The route choice is authorized as a detailed-design choice, while the identified concerns are missing producer/ownership semantics and cross-document consistency.

The lifecycle clearly requires W02 destroy before GuestRam release, serializes Guest setup before Guest execution, uses deterministic zero-fill, and treats mappings as W02 state. It deliberately retains a single test convention and denies any permanent ABI; findings concern address/resource binding and grant shape.

The pre-copy bounds proof, checked arithmetic, Guest-side defensive boot-info parsing, consuming release requiring W02 destroy proof, and single bounded unsafe writer provide good guards. The design says bad host-authored layout is fatal, so the VM-facing label is overbroad rather than suggesting actual panic on untrusted Guest data.

Workflow includes explicit stop conditions for missing allocator continuity, missing ownership extension and missing Host mapping; it assigns evidence to W08 and keeps changes within selected design. This limits risk but the implementation-entry wording and unresolved cross-package shapes need correction before coding.

The validation matrix distinguishes W03 logic from allocator correctness/P2 evidence, requires explicit blocked/not-run status, and keeps P2-ACR-01 unresolved. No row is represented as passed before a verification record exists.

The design is proposed and routes RAM only through P2 allocator, labels layout/console as temporary test conventions, calls P2 ownership and P1 Host mapping assumptions out, and forbids machine-ABI claims. The task book requires an image route/layout but does not itself authorize an MMIO passthrough mechanism; no implementation is claimed.

acceptance_to_evidence.acceptance: P5-V03, V09, V10, and V13 require evidence that required valid and invalid Guest-data cases receive controlled outcomes without unchecked Host access or an unexplained Hypervisor failure. This does not prove IPC or general shared memory.
Implementation, failures and handoff must be recorded only when work actually starts/completes.

counterevidence: Decision 8 openly excludes concurrent Stage-2 mutation and reserves P3 shootdown; AC-03.2 fails closed on protected translation. This is useful counterevidence for mapping mutation only, not guest data writes or whole-VM quiescence.

The design expressly gates the Arch binding on AC-03.3 and makes post-validation Host fault an invariant; it states Guest inputs remain untrusted and the Guest sees no partial result after invariant. This still does not guarantee snapshot consistency against another vCPU.

AC-03.2 assumes Stage-2 never maps any P2-protected range to a Guest, and guard is described as belt-and-braces. If P2 guarantees protected extents are page-aligned, the base check may suffice; the design should cite that exact guarantee. QueryUnavailable is expressly not a Guest fault, so it cannot double as unmapped without changing failure semantics.

Accessors iterate only validated segments and use no Guest-supplied pointer; AC-03.3 makes host-side page access fault an invariant. This protects address bounds but does not serialize the Guest's other vCPUs.
Workflow blocks binding when AC-03.1/AC-03.3 are not evidenced, requires fake-space coverage and stepwise all-or-nothing checks, and prohibits scope leakage into W06.

DV04 is explicitly blocked on live P4/W07 prerequisites, and Known limitations explicitly exclude concurrent Stage-2 mutation. That narrows claims about mapping changes; concurrent data writes still need a stated boundary.

W03 explicitly reserves concurrent Stage-2 mutation and requires future TLB-shootdown integration; its access is two-phase and copy routines consume validated segments only. That addresses translation mutation policy partially but not concurrent guest writes from another vCPU. Runtime design remains proposed.

findings.candidate: Decision 7 says 'the Guest is stopped (it issued the hypercall)' to justify capture-then-use, but this establishes only that vCPU, not every vCPU of the VM. W02 explicitly permits concurrent vCPUs, so a second vCPU may write data or alter mappings during this operation. Specify the isolation/quiescence/snapshot guarantee.
findings.classification: detailed-design contract candidate; not proof of implementation defect

counterevidence: The design makes stale-reference rejection and serialized access explicit, and DV06 includes concurrency tests. The findings are pseudocode gaps relative to those stated invariants, not a proposed relaxation of the security rule.
The architecture states the desired linearization and retire invariants plainly; companion pseudocode needs to match them. W04 is only a proposed design.

The codec validates the 24-bit slot against capacity and defined class tags, and table invariants require monotonically increasing generation/retired slots. No direct inconsistency beyond lifecycle pseudocode in companion 04 was found here.

Table-wide locking and class-tag checking are explicitly required; the cascade is intended as one transaction and emitted events occur after unlock. But those statements do not resolve the missing class check/referent lookup or generation-overflow path in the pseudocode.
Workflow requires full operation corpora, invariant checking, and no stale acceptance, so it can be expanded to cover these edge interleavings without changing package scope.

DV01 also requires destroy/reuse stale-handle rejection and DV02 checks cascade atomicity; those cover nearby but not the interleaving between validation and lock reacquisition. The design remains proposed and has not passed these tests.

The proposal explicitly requires one table-wide lock, says lookups/destroy are serialized, and mandates retire-on-wrap; intended invariants are sound, but the listed pseudocode does not preserve them through the validation-lock gap/wrap edge. These remain proposed contracts.

acceptance_to_evidence.acceptance: P5-V06–V08 require evidence that an explicitly granted caller succeeds only within its rights, identity shortcuts never authorize, and revoked authority cannot be reused. Passing does not prove delegation, a policy engine, or a Control Domain.
Implementation, failures and handoff must be recorded only when work actually starts/completes.

counterevidence: Decision 6's generation binding ensures authority never matches a recreated object; Decision 8 explicitly avoids nested locks. This resolves stale future lookups, not necessarily a call already past authorization. Clarify in-flight-call semantics.
No W04/W05 locks are nested and revoke/authorize share one lock, so their state transition itself is linearizable. This protects check outcomes while leaving post-check effects open.

Rights are non-Guest-visible, only defined bits are accepted, Delegate is not grantable, and W05 refuses to re-decode handles; it expects W04-validated target shapes. No additional direct mismatch confirmed.

The sequential grant→authorize→revoke→authorize test correctly expects later checks to be denied, and the tombstone path is one-way. The ambiguity concerns a call already authorized concurrently before revoke.
Step 6 is explicit about the never-nested lock rule and labels W06 as owner of ordering. W06 can own the resolution, but it must consume a clarified W05 lifetime/revocation guarantee.
DV06 appropriately limits claims to the designed concurrency boundary and forbids scalability claims; W05 remains proposed and no race test is claimed.

W05 requires exact target generation binding; destroyed-generation records cannot authorize new uses, and W04 lock is never nested with W05 lock. Its matrix tests revoke-vs-authorize. Those protect table lookups but do not settle in-flight operations after the lock is released.

findings.candidate: Decision 8 allows the sequence W04 validation/release → W05 authorize/release → execute, while W04 may destroy target after validation and W05 may revoke after authorization. Because I-1 mirrors P7-W06 block handshake and prior P7-W06 review found a lost-wakeup interleaving (intent → empty poll → event publication → waker observes Running → blocker commits Blocked), the shared producer/consumer protocol needs owner-level redesign/reconciliation before W08 can claim no lost idle wake. W08 currently does not define a stable contract that breaks this dependency.

P3-W07 and P6-W04 source contracts, architectural wait seam, placement/online CPU identity, and W05/W02 delivered queue/lifecycle interfaces are not proven by this plan/design. W08 must not implement substitute transports, timer, Core WFE, placement or queue semantics.

All W08-DV01..DV11 and P7-V17/V18 are planned only. No implementation or verification records/evidence are present in the reviewed design handoff; QEMU evidence would not establish real hardware WFE or interrupt-latency behavior.
